subject: Using Lavaan to compare two indirect and one direct pathway with some quadratic relationships

messages.author: 8ceb46a7782e467e
messages.subject: Using Lavaan to compare two indirect and one direct pathway with some quadratic relationships
parts:
Dear Lavaan Group,
   I am a graduate student, new to Lavaan, and really appreciate any help.  I am hoping to determine if variable A (continuous variable) affects variable D (a binary, factor variable) either directly or indirectly through variable B (a continuous variable) or variable C (a binary, factor variable).  One problem I have is  that the relationship is quadratic between A and D and also between B and D (all other relationships are linear).  I am a little confused on how to include these quadratic variables in Lavaan.    I am hoping to compare these three pathways (one direct and two indirect) with AIC.  I have seen the postings for determining one indirect pathway but am unsure of how to compare two indirect pathways (with each other and also with the direct pathway).  I've attached part of my data and the model I am hoping to examine.  I've included my coding attempts below although I have been unable to correct the error message it is giving for looking at indirect/direct effects (error: "missing observed variables in dataset").  I may be missing something, but as far as I understand, I have defined these variables in my model.  Thank you for any feedback/ideas,
Ellen

data=read.csv("Ellen_data.csv")

data$Aquad=data$A^2  #get quadratic of A
data$Bquad=(data$B^2)/100  #Get quadratic of B. 
                                                #I divided by 100 to make the variance more comparable with other variables
#the overall model
model='D~A+Aquad+B+Bquad+C
             B~A
             C~A'
fit=sem(model,data=data,fixed.x=F)
summary(fit)

#get direct/indirect/total effects
model_all='D~A*a+Aquad*d+B*b+Bquad*d+C*c
             B~A*f
             C~A*g
            direct:=a*d
            indirect1:=f*b*d
            indirect2:=g*c
            total:= (a*d)+(f*b*d)+(g*c)'
fit_all=sem(model_all,data=data,fixed.x=F)
summary(fit_all)
AICc(fit_all)

#first indirect pathway
model_indirect1='C~A*g
             D~A*a+Aquad*d+C*c
            indirect:=g*c
            direct:=a*d
            total:=(g*c)+(a*d)'
fit_indirect1=sem(model_indirect1,data=data,fixed.x=F)
summary(fit_indirect1)
AICc(fit_indirect1)

#second indirect pathway
model_indirect2='B~A*f
             D~A*a+Aquad*d+B*b+Bquad*d
            indirect:=f*b*d
            direct:=a*d
            total:=(f*b*d)+(a*d)'
fit_indirect2=sem(model_indirect2,data=data,fixed.x=F)
summary(fit_indirect2)
AICc(fit_indirect2)

#direct pathway only
model_direct='D~A+Aquad'
fit_direct=sem(model_direct,data=data,fixed.x=F)
summary(fit_direct)
AICc(fit_direct)

#compare the three pathways
model.sel(fit_indirect1,fit_indirect2,fit_direct)

messages.subject: Re: Using Lavaan to compare two indirect and one direct pathway with some quadratic relationships
parts: I am hoping to compare these three pathways (one direct and two indirect) with AIC.
AIC is for comparing models (with the same data, but not the same parameters, or even the same parameterization), not for comparing parameter estimates.
I have seen the postings for determining one indirect pathway but am unsure of how to compare two indirect pathways (with each other and also with the direct pathway).

You already defined parameters indirect1 and indirect2.  If you want to test whether their difference is zero (i.e., the null hypothesis  that they are the same), you can define a parameter for their difference as well.  For example:

indirectDiff := indirect1 - indirect2

B~A*f
             C~A*g
            direct:=a*d
            indirect1:=f*b*d
            indirect2:=g*c
            total:= (a*d)+(f*b*d)+(g*c)'

You need to put the labels before the variable names, not after.  lavaan interprets 'D~A*a' as the effect of variable a on variable D (labeled A), not the effect of A on D (labeled a).

Terry
